angle: In Durham Region a hot tub is what the 401 and the GO train are for: it is the reward waiting in the backyard when a long commute finally ends, often on a lot so new the sod has not knit together yet.

hot-tub.intro: Every tub on this page is priced as it sits on our Dundas Street East floor, minutes off the 401. Below the listings you will find what matters when a tub goes into a Whitby, Oshawa, Ajax or Clarington yard.
body: Winter along the north shore of Lake Ontario is less about deep snow and more about wind, freezing rain and a damp cold that follows you from the GO platform to the car. That weather is why tubs here run twelve months a year. A cover with locking straps matters more in Pickering and Ajax, where the southwest wind comes off the water, than in Brooklin or Uxbridge, where snow load is the bigger concern. Full foam insulation and a cover lifter pay for themselves by February. Right now every new 2026 Jacuzzi in stock is 20% off in our Red Tag inventory clearance, not combinable with other offers.

North Whitby, Brooklin, Courtice and north Bowmanville are full of new builds with fresh sod, a rear yard forty or forty five feet wide, a gate in the side fence and the electrical panel in a basement close to the back wall. We measure the gate before we quote, because a tub travels on its edge on a dolly and some gates need a fence panel lifted out for the afternoon. Older Oshawa and south Ajax streets are the opposite: mature trees, a detached garage and a narrow side yard, which sometimes means a crane. Fresh sod on heavy clay needs a proper pad, never pavers on bare ground.

The typical buyer here parks at Whitby, Oshawa, Ajax or Pickering GO before seven and gets home after six, so the tub has to be hot without anyone thinking about it. A J-335 or J-375 with a good cover holds temperature all day. Families in Courtice and Bowmanville with a bigger lot lean toward the seven seat J-385 or J-485. GM shift workers and Lakeridge Health staff coming off nights soak at odd hours, and the Nordic Retreat All-In-110V suits a Scugog or Uxbridge property where hydro is tight. If your water comes from a well, tell us so we can set up water care for hardness and iron.

faq.q: Can I start heating the tub from the GO train so it is ready when I get home?
faq.a: On J-400 and J-500 series tubs the SmartTub app lets you check the water temperature and adjust the set point from your phone, so you can nudge it up from the Lakeshore East line. In practice most owners leave the tub at soaking temperature around the clock; a well insulated Jacuzzi loses very little heat under a locked cover. Nordic and Aquasolus tubs do not have app control, so keep them at temperature rather than reheating from cold.

faq.q: My new build was just graded and sodded. How soon can a tub go in?
faq.a: Talk to your builder first, because many new home warranties expect the final grade to stay undisturbed for a period, and any pad must not block the drainage swale between houses. Once the yard has settled through a few good rains, a poured concrete pad or a compacted gravel base on a level cut will carry the weight. Pavers set on fresh sod will heave the first spring.

faq.q: Will a hot tub fit through the gate in a standard subdivision fence?
faq.a: Often, but not always. A tub rides on its side on a dolly, so we need roughly the tub's height in clear width, nothing overhead and a straight run to the pad. Many new-build gates in Brooklin and Courtice are too narrow, so our crew lifts out a fence panel and puts it back the same day. Where the houses are too close for that, a crane from the street lifts the tub over the roof.

faq.q: Do I need a permit or a fence for a hot tub in Durham Region?
faq.a: Each municipality writes its own rules, and Whitby, Oshawa, Ajax, Pickering, Clarington, Scugog and Uxbridge do not all treat a hot tub the same way. Some require a pool enclosure permit unless the tub has a locking cover, and setbacks from property lines and easements vary. Call your town's building department before you pour a pad; we can tell you what we have seen on recent installs in your area.

faq.q: Does well water change how I look after the tub?
faq.a: Yes. Rural properties around Port Perry, Uxbridge and north Clarington often have hard water with dissolved iron, which stains shells and clouds water if you fill straight from the hose. Use a fill filter, test the source water and add a metal sequestrant on the first fill. Municipal water in Whitby, Oshawa, Ajax and Pickering comes treated from Lake Ontario and needs only the standard start up.

swim-spa.intro: A swim spa gives a Durham family a lane to swim in January and a place to soak afterward, in a footprint that fits the rear yard of a new build. Every price below is what you would pay at our Whitby showroom.
body: In-ground pools used to be the default in older Oshawa and Ajax neighbourhoods with deep lots. The subdivisions going up in north Whitby, Brooklin, Courtice and Bowmanville are a different shape: shorter yards, houses closer together, and a grading plan you cannot dig through without a conversation with the builder. A 14 foot swim spa such as the Jacuzzi J-14 PowerActive at $41,395 sits above ground or half sunk along the fence line and leaves the rest of the yard for the kids. There is no closing in October and no opening in May, which matters when both parents commute.

Who buys a swim spa here: triathletes and runners who train on the Waterfront Trail in Ajax and Pickering and want to swim without driving to a pool, Ontario Tech and Durham College staff who have settled in north Oshawa, and parents who want lessons at home. The Jacuzzi PowerPro line has the strongest current for a serious swimmer; the J-16 PowerPro is $54,295. Families who mostly want a warm pool the kids can play in look at the J-13 PowerPlay with eight seats at $33,195. The SwimLife SwimExpert DualStream 19 at $56,095 adds an attached five person hot tub with its own controls.

Delivery in Durham is a crane job on nearly every swim spa, and in a new subdivision the crane usually sets up on the street and lifts over the house. We check for overhead hydro lines, the distance from curb to pad and the condition of the driveway before we book. The pad is a reinforced concrete slab poured on compacted base, sized for the shell and thousands of litres of water, and the electrical run to a new-build panel is typically short. On rural lots in Scugog or Uxbridge with well water, plan on a fill filter and a longer first balance.

faq.q: Will a swim spa fit on a forty foot lot in Brooklin or Courtice?
faq.a: Usually, with a 14 foot model set parallel to the rear fence. Measure from the back wall of the house to the rear property line and subtract the setback your municipality requires; most new-build rear yards leave enough for a 14 footer plus a walkway. The 16 and 19 foot models are more often a fit on older Oshawa lots or rural properties.

faq.q: How does a swim spa get into a backyard when the houses are only a few feet apart?
faq.a: By crane, in almost every case. The truck parks on the street or in the driveway, the operator lifts the spa over the roofline and sets it on the pad in about an hour. We do a site visit first to confirm there are no hydro lines in the way and that the crane has a level place to stand. Older streets with a laneway or a double driveway to the back sometimes allow a forklift instead.

faq.q: Is a swim spa treated like a pool under local fence bylaws?
faq.a: In most Durham municipalities a swim spa holds enough water to count as a pool, which brings an enclosure permit and fence height rules into play, and a locking cover may or may not satisfy them. Whitby, Clarington, Oshawa and Pickering each set their own requirements. Confirm with the building department before ordering, and bring the dimensions of the model you are considering.

faq.q: Can I really swim outside in Durham in January?
faq.a: Yes, and many owners say winter is when they use it most. The water sits at whatever temperature you set and the cover keeps it there between sessions. Keep a clear path shovelled from the door, set the spa where the house or fence breaks the prevailing wind, and add a floating thermal blanket under the hard cover to cut heat loss on the coldest nights.

faq.q: Which swim spa suits a competitive swimmer versus a family?
faq.a: A swimmer training for open water events off the Ajax or Pickering waterfront wants the Jacuzzi PowerPro current, and the J-19 PowerPro at $58,995 gives the most room to stretch out. A family that wants a warm pool and a place to sit chooses seats over current; the J-12 Flow with eight seats is $30,695. The SwimLife SwimFit SwimStream 14 at $38,095 is the value pick for a swimmer on a smaller lot.

sauna.intro: Sauna culture arrived in Durham with the wellness crowd and the shift workers, and it fits the housing here: a Clearlight infrared cabin in a Brooklin basement or a Serenity cedar sauna on a Scugog lot.
body: Most saunas we deliver in Whitby, Ajax, Pickering and Oshawa go indoors. New builds come with an unfinished basement and full height ceilings, and a Clearlight Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 assembles in an afternoon in the corner of that basement without any renovation. Townhomes and semis in Ajax and north Oshawa have less floor area, and the Sanctuary 1 at $10,495 fits where a treadmill would. A finished basement bedroom or the space beside the furnace room works too. Check the door width, the ceiling height and the location of the nearest outlet before you buy, and we will tell you which cabin fits.

Outdoor cedar saunas belong on the bigger properties: Lake Scugog waterfront near Port Perry, rolling moraine acreage around Uxbridge, farm lots in north Clarington and the older deep lots in Bowmanville and Newcastle. The Serenity Sauna at $17,495 and the smaller Serenity Mini at $14,995 are built from Western red cedar, and the heater is sold separately so you can choose electric or wood burning. A wood burner suits a rural lot where running a new 240V line to the back of the property would cost more than the sauna itself. Set it on a level gravel or concrete base and check with the township about accessory structures.

Who uses a sauna in Durham: GM employees coming off a shift, nurses and paramedics from Lakeridge Health, hockey parents standing in cold arenas three nights a week, and cyclists and runners who train along the lake. Many pair the sauna with a Chill Tubs cold plunge for a contrast routine, and the Sanctuary 2, Sanctuary 3 and Sanctuary Y are the cabins we most often deliver alongside one. Both types are running on our Dundas Street East floor, so you can sit in the infrared heat and stand inside the cedar before deciding.

faq.q: Where do most people put an infrared sauna in a Durham new build?
faq.a: The basement, almost always. New builds in Brooklin, Courtice and Bowmanville come with unfinished basements and enough ceiling height for every Clearlight Sanctuary model. Place it near an outlet, leave a few inches behind it for airflow and set it on the concrete or a finished floor, never on carpet underlay that traps moisture.

faq.q: Can I run a wood-burning Serenity sauna on a Lake Scugog or Uxbridge property?
faq.a: Yes, and it is one of the best uses of a rural lot. A wood burning heater needs no hydro, which is a real advantage when the sauna sits well away from the house. Ask the Township of Scugog or Uxbridge about accessory buildings and chimney clearances before you pour the base, and keep firewood dry under cover through the freezing rain season.

faq.q: What base does an outdoor sauna need on a lot with fresh sod?
faq.a: A level, well drained base that keeps the cedar off wet ground: compacted gravel with patio stones, a concrete pad or a small deck all work. Fresh sod on Durham clay will settle unevenly for a season, so do not set the sauna directly on the lawn. Keep the base clear of the drainage swale that runs between new houses.

faq.q: Will a cedar sauna stand up to the wind and freezing rain off Lake Ontario?
faq.a: Western red cedar is the traditional outdoor sauna wood for exactly this reason: it resists rot and stays stable through wet and dry cycles. In Ajax and Pickering, where the southwest wind comes off the water, face the door away from the prevailing wind and anchor the sauna to its base. A coat of exterior finish on the roof and exposed ends every couple of seasons keeps it looking new.

faq.q: How do you get a Serenity sauna into a fenced subdivision yard?
faq.a: Much more easily than a hot tub. Serenity saunas arrive as panels and are assembled on the base in your yard, so they pass through a standard gate one piece at a time with no crane and no fence panel removal. Allow a day for assembly and a visit from your electrician afterward if you chose an electric heater.

hot-tub.small: Three and four seat tubs and the Nordic 110V models are the answer for the narrow side yards of older Oshawa streets, the townhome patios in Ajax and Pickering, and any Scugog or Uxbridge property where the hydro service is already spoken for. The Jacuzzi J-315 at $18,795 is a three seat tub with the same shell quality as the big ones. The Nordic Sport All-In-110V at $7,295 and Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 plug into a dedicated outlet and skip the panel upgrade. The Aquasolus The Brook at $10,995 seats four and includes White Glove delivery and setup.
hot-tub.medium: Five and six seat tubs are the sweet spot for a Brooklin, Courtice or north Whitby new build where the yard is forty five feet wide and two adults and two kids use it most nights. The Jacuzzi J-335 at $21,995 is our most common pick for a commuter household. The J-375 at $25,295 adds jets, and the J-445 has floor model clearance stock at $23,995. On a tighter budget the Aquasolus The Eden at $13,995 seats six, and the Jacuzzi J-275 is on clearance from $14,695 while 2025 stock lasts.
hot-tub.large: Seven seats and up suits the bigger Bowmanville and Newcastle lots, the multigenerational households in north Oshawa and Ajax, and anyone who hosts the hockey team. The Jacuzzi J-509 seats eight with 76 jets at $39,595, and the J-495 seats nine with floor model clearance at $31,395. The J-385 at $26,595 is the seven seat choice most families land on. Our own Wellness Shop Ontario S106 at $17,695 gives you seven seats and two 6-HP jet pumps, and the Aquasolus The Cove at $11,995 is the lowest priced seven seater we carry, with delivery included.

productNotes.swim-spa: Swim spas in Durham go to the families who skipped the in-ground pool because the new-build yard was too short, and to the athletes training for events along the Lake Ontario shore. The 14 foot Jacuzzi J-14 PowerActive at $41,395 is the fit for a subdivision lot; the 19 foot J-19DT PowerPro at $60,895 gives a Scugog or Uxbridge property a full lane and a separate hot tub end. Plan on a crane over the roof in Brooklin and Courtice and a reinforced slab wherever it lands.
productNotes.sauna: Infrared cabins go into the basements of Whitby, Ajax and Pickering new builds and townhomes, and the Clearlight Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 is the one we deliver most. Outdoor cedar goes to Port Perry, Uxbridge, north Clarington and the deep lots of old Bowmanville, where the Serenity Sauna at $17,495 with a wood burning heater needs no hydro at all. Come feel both on the Dundas Street East floor before you choose.
productNotes.cold-plunge: Chill Tubs cold plunges have found a following among GM shift workers, Lakeridge Health staff and the hockey and lacrosse crowd across Durham who want a contrast routine at home. The Essential Bath and Essential Pod fit on a patio or in a garage; the Obsidian and Pro are the step up. Pricing is in the showroom, and we can quote an Essential together with a Clearlight Sanctuary 2, 3 or Y. Cold water in a Durham January is easy; the chiller earns its keep in July.

financing: A lot of Durham buyers are newly in a house in Brooklin, Courtice, Bowmanville or north Oshawa, with a fresh mortgage and a yard that still needs a fence and a deck. Financing lets the tub go in this season instead of three years from now, with a bi-weekly payment that lines up with a paycheque from GM, the hospital, the school board or a Toronto office reached by GO. The Nordic Sport All-In-110V starts from $15.01 bi-weekly and the Retreat All-In-110V from $18.62. Ask about current promotional terms on approved credit at the Dundas Street East showroom or on any product page.
showroom: You will find us at 1549 Dundas Street East, Unit 3, in Whitby, just north of Highway 401 and a few minutes from the Whitby GO. Take the Thickson Road exit off the 401, head north to Dundas Street and we are a short drive along Dundas East, with parking out front. Jacuzzi, Nordic, Aquasolus and Wellness Shop Ontario hot tubs are filled and running on the floor, a swim spa is heated for swim tests, and Clearlight and Serenity saunas are set up so you can sit inside them.

Bring your measurements: the width of your gate, the distance from the back door to where the tub will sit, and a photo of your panel. Ajax, Pickering, Oshawa and Clarington shoppers make up most of our traffic, and we can usually tell you within an hour which models will fit your yard and your service. Wet tests are welcome, so bring a swimsuit and a towel, and a weekday evening after the GO train gets in is often the quietest time to try three or four tubs back to back.

Oshawa.lead: Oshawa is our closest neighbour and the largest city in Durham, with everything from postwar bungalows south of the 401 to new subdivisions around Ontario Tech and Durham College in the north end.
body: The older neighbourhoods near downtown and the harbour have deep, narrow lots with detached garages, mature maples and a side yard that may be four feet wide, which means we measure carefully and sometimes bring a crane. North Oshawa, from Taunton Road up past the university, is newer: wider frontages, a rear gate and a basement panel near the back wall, so delivery is a dolly through the gate and a short electrical run. Between the two are the sixties and seventies streets with big backyards and a 100 amp service that an ESA licensed electrician should assess before you buy a 60 amp tub.

GM families, Lakeridge Health staff on rotating shifts and the university and college community are our Oshawa customers, along with a growing number of Toronto commuters who parked at Oshawa GO and never left. Shift workers soak at odd hours and like the app control on the J-400 series; a J-435 at $27,895, or the floor model clearance at $24,995, fits the budget of a two income household. Parents of students in the north end buy the J-345 seven seater at $23,195 because it handles a full house at Thanksgiving, and the older streets take a J-315 where the side yard rules out anything wider.
Oshawa.drive: From downtown Oshawa take King Street west, which becomes Dundas Street once you cross into Whitby; we are about ten minutes along. From the north end, Thickson Road south from Taunton is quickest.

Ajax.lead: Ajax runs from the Lake Ontario waterfront north past the 401 and Taunton Road, and the split between the older south end and the newer north end shapes almost every delivery we do there.
body: South Ajax, around Harwood Avenue and the waterfront, has the wartime and postwar housing the town was built on: modest lots, detached homes close together and side yards that were never meant for a hot tub on a dolly. Many of these deliveries are a crane from the street, and the panel is often an older 100 amp service. North Ajax, above Rossland Road and along Salem and Audley, is newer subdivision housing with rear gates and 200 amp panels. Waterfront properties get the full force of the southwest wind, so cover straps and a windbreak matter more here than anywhere else we deliver.

Ajax buyers are overwhelmingly commuters, either on the Lakeshore East line from Ajax GO or in the 401 crawl toward Scarborough, and they want a tub that is hot at seven in the evening without any effort. The J-335 at $21,995 and the J-355 at $24,795 are the most common picks in the north end. Townhome owners near the GO station look at the three seat J-215 at $14,095 or a Nordic Retreat SE at $10,195 on a patio. A Clearlight Sanctuary 1 in a townhome basement is a popular add on for the fitness crowd who run the Waterfront Trail.
Ajax.drive: Take Highway 401 east to the Thickson Road exit, then north to Dundas Street, about fifteen minutes from Ajax GO. Kingston Road east becomes Dundas Street at the Whitby border and leads straight to us.

Pickering.lead: Pickering stretches from Frenchman's Bay and the lakefront up through the 401 corridor to the new Seaton community north of Highway 407 and the farm country around Claremont.
body: The waterfront streets around Frenchman's Bay and Bay Ridges are older, with tighter lots and a wind off the lake that will lift an unstrapped cover; we recommend a cover lifter, locking straps and placing the tub in the lee of the house or garage. Central Pickering between the 401 and Finch Avenue has the wide suburban lots of the seventies and eighties, an easy dolly delivery and room for a big tub. Seaton, north of the 407, is brand new: fresh sod, small rear yards, narrow gates and a builder grading plan you need to respect when you choose the pad location.

Pickering is our westernmost service area and the one with the most Toronto commuters, whether they board at Pickering GO or drive the 401 to Scarborough or downtown. They buy a J-375 at $25,295 or a J-408L at $29,995 with the SmartTub app so the water is exactly right when they walk in the door. Retirees in the lakeside bungalows go smaller and quieter, often the four seat J-404L at $25,195. Rural properties around Claremont on well water need a fill filter and a look at the hydro service before a 240V tub goes in.
Pickering.drive: Highway 401 east to Thickson Road, then north to Dundas Street, takes about twenty five minutes from Pickering Town Centre. From Seaton, the 407 to the 412 and south to Dundas is quicker.

Bowmanville.lead: Bowmanville is Clarington's main town, with a historic downtown along King Street, deep older lots around it and new subdivisions climbing the hills to the north and spreading east and west.
body: The streets around downtown Bowmanville have the deepest backyards in our territory: century homes and postwar houses on lots that run back far enough for a swim spa, a sauna and a tub. Those yards often have a driveway to a rear garage, which makes delivery simple. The subdivisions on the north side of town toward the 418 and Highway 407 are new builds with fresh sod, forty to forty five foot frontages, gates that may need a panel lifted out and basements that were unfinished on closing. Clay soils here heave in the spring thaw, so a proper pad is not optional.

Bowmanville buyers are young families who moved east for a detached house and now drive the 401 or the 418 to the 407 for work, plus longtime residents upgrading a twenty year old tub. The seven seat J-385 at $26,595 and J-485 at $30,795 are the common family picks, and the eight seat J-509 at $39,595 shows up on the big downtown lots. The J-13 PowerPlay swim spa at $33,195 has replaced more than one planned pool here. Outdoor Serenity saunas go on the acreages north of town, where well water and a wood burning heater both make sense.
Bowmanville.drive: Highway 401 west to Thickson Road, then north to Dundas Street, roughly twenty minutes from downtown Bowmanville. Highway 2 west through Courtice and Oshawa is the slower route that ends at our front door.

Courtice.lead: Courtice sits between Oshawa and Bowmanville along Highway 2, and it has grown from a crossroads into one of the busiest new-build markets in Durham, with the 418 now at its doorstep.
body: Nearly every Courtice delivery is a new or nearly new house: two storeys, a rear yard of modest depth, a fence that went up the summer after closing and a gate that is often too narrow for a tub on its side. We lift out a fence panel, roll the tub through and rebuild the fence the same afternoon. The panel is in the basement near the back wall, so the electrical run is short and the ESA inspection straightforward. Older homes along Courtice Road and Nash Road have bigger yards, mature trees and sometimes a septic bed to steer clear of.

The people buying here are commuters using the 401 or the 418 to the 407, dual income households with school age kids, and a growing number of grandparents who followed the family east. A six seat J-335 at $21,995 or a J-345 seven seater at $23,195 is the typical first tub, and the Aquasolus The Calma at $13,995 with delivery included is a common choice when the deck and fence have already eaten the budget. Clearlight Sanctuary 2 cabins go into the unfinished basements, often with a Chill Tubs Essential beside them.
Courtice.drive: Highway 2 west through Oshawa becomes King Street and then Dundas Street in Whitby, about fifteen minutes without traffic. The 401 west to Thickson Road is faster at rush hour.

Brooklin.lead: Brooklin is the fast growing north end of Whitby along Baldwin Street, a village core surrounded by new subdivisions and a Highway 407 interchange that turned it into commuter country.
body: The village core around Baldwin and Winchester has older homes on generous lots with room for a tub and a sauna, and a few of them are still on well water. Everything around it is new: crescents of two storey homes with forty to fifty foot frontages, fresh sod, wood fences with three foot gates and rear yards that back onto another rear yard. Expect a fence panel to come out on delivery day and expect the ground to settle for a season before the final landscaping. The panel is in the basement, and 200 amp service is standard, so a 60 amp tub is rarely a problem.

Brooklin buyers commute on the 407 to Markham and Vaughan or take the 412 down to the 401 and the Whitby GO, and they are usually a family with young kids and a new house that still needs a deck. The J-335 at $21,995 is our best seller here; the J-375 at $25,295 and the J-435 at $27,895 follow. Swim spas are gaining ground because the lots are too short for a pool, and the J-14 PowerActive at $41,395 fits. A Clearlight Sanctuary 3 at $12,995 in the basement rounds out the wellness setup.
Brooklin.drive: Head south on Baldwin Street, which becomes Brock Street in downtown Whitby, then east on Dundas Street; about fifteen minutes. Or take the 407 to the 412 and exit at Dundas.

Port Perry.lead: Port Perry is the lakeside town at the heart of Scugog, with a heritage main street on Lake Scugog and rural roads, farms and waterfront lots spreading out in every direction.
body: In town the lots are older and level, with municipal water and a gate you can usually get a tub through. Outside town it is a different job: long gravel driveways, sloped waterfront on Scugog Island and the west shore, hydro that comes down a long line from the road and water from a drilled well. We plan those deliveries around the seasons, because a soft spring driveway will not carry a crane, and we bring a fill filter because well water around here often runs hard with iron. A 240V tub far from the house may need a subpanel, which your ESA licensed electrician will price.

Port Perry customers are retirees who sold in Toronto or Whitby for a lake view, cottage owners turning the place into a year round home, and farm families who want a soak after chores. The Nordic Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 is popular on the cottage properties where hydro is limited, and the J-365 seven seater at $24,795 goes on the lake lots where the grandchildren visit. The Serenity Sauna at $17,495 with a wood burning heater is a natural fit on acreage, and the view over Lake Scugog from a cedar sauna is hard to beat in January.
Port Perry.drive: Take Highway 7A west to Highway 12, then south through Brooklin into Whitby, where Baldwin Street becomes Brock Street; turn east on Dundas. Allow about thirty five minutes, or use Simcoe Street south through Oshawa.

Clarington.lead: Clarington covers Courtice, Bowmanville, Newcastle and Orono plus a broad rural north of farms, hamlets and moraine country, so no two Clarington deliveries look alike.
body: The urban parts of Clarington are covered on our Courtice, Bowmanville and Newcastle pages. The rural municipality is where Clarington gets interesting for us: hamlets like Hampton, Enniskillen and Tyrone with older homes on big lots, farm properties with outbuildings and long drives, and estate lots on the moraine with a well, a septic system and hydro that may already be working hard. We look at the service before recommending a tub, and a Nordic 110V model or a wood fired Serenity sauna sidesteps the problem entirely. Winter access down an unplowed lane decides delivery timing.

Rural Clarington buyers are farm families, tradespeople who work across Durham and Toronto and wanted land, and retirees who left Oshawa or Scarborough for quiet. They use the tub after a day outdoors and they want it big and simple: the Wellness Shop Ontario S104 seven seater at $15,595 and the Aquasolus The Cove at $11,995 both do the job without fuss. Well water is the rule, so every rural fill gets a filter and a metal sequestrant. Outdoor Serenity saunas and Chill Tubs cold plunges fit the space and the lifestyle, and a wood burning heater keeps the hydro bill where it was.
Clarington.drive: From the hamlets north of Bowmanville take Regional Road 57 or Highway 35/115 south to the 401, west to Thickson Road and north to Dundas; thirty to forty minutes depending on where you start.

Uxbridge.lead: Uxbridge sits on the Oak Ridges Moraine at the north edge of Durham, a town known for its trails, surrounded by horse farms, estate lots and hardwood hills.
body: The town itself has older homes on serviced lots and newer subdivisions on the edges, and both are straightforward deliveries. The estate and farm properties outside town are where planning matters: rolling terrain, long tree lined drives, wells with hard water, and winters that bring more snow than the lakeshore because of the elevation. A tub on a moraine hillside needs a properly levelled pad cut into the slope, and the cover needs to shed real snow load. We schedule rural Uxbridge deliveries for firm ground, either frozen midwinter or dry summer, never during the spring thaw.

Uxbridge buyers are equestrians and hobby farmers, trail runners and cyclists, and 407 commuters who wanted acreage within reach of Markham. They lean toward big, quiet tubs like the J-485 at $30,795 or the J-475 with 55 jets at the same price, and they are the most likely customers in Durham to add a Serenity cedar sauna with a wood burning heater. On properties where the hydro is limited, the Nordic Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 runs on a dedicated outlet. Ask about a subpanel if the tub sits far from the house.
Uxbridge.drive: Take Lake Ridge Road south the whole way, then Dundas Street east through downtown Whitby, or use Highway 47 to Highway 12 and Baldwin Street; about forty minutes either way.

Newcastle.lead: Newcastle is the village at the east end of our territory, with a heritage main street on King Avenue, older homes on deep lots and newer subdivisions between the village and the Port of Newcastle on the lake.
body: Village lots in Newcastle are among the easiest deliveries we do: level, deep, often with a driveway to a rear garage and room for a seven seater plus a sauna. The newer streets toward the harbour are compact new builds with tight gates, fresh sod and a lake wind that comes straight up from the water, so cover straps and placement out of the wind matter. North of the 401 the properties turn rural quickly, with wells and long drives. It is a long run from Whitby for our crews, so we group Newcastle and Bowmanville deliveries on the same day when we can.

Newcastle buyers are a mix of retirees who wanted a small town with a marina, families priced east along the 401, and boaters who split the summer between the harbour and the backyard. The J-285 seven seater at $18,695 and the J-345 at $23,195 are the value picks on the village lots, and the J-508 at $35,695 goes to the buyer who wants the top of the line on a lot big enough to show it off. Rural buyers north of the village choose Serenity saunas and Chill Tubs plunges to go with the tub.
Newcastle.drive: Highway 401 west from the Mill Street interchange to Thickson Road in Whitby, then north to Dundas Street; about twenty five to thirty minutes.

productBlurbs.j-509: Eight open seats around 76 PowerPro jets need a yard to match, and the deep century lots around downtown Bowmanville, with a driveway to the back for delivery, are where the J-509 usually lands. Grandparents, teenagers and the neighbours fit at once without anyone perched on an edge. It is the tub for the household that hosts every long weekend, with ProClarity 6-Stage filtration built to keep up. Sale price $39,595, and the Red Tag 20% comes off at the counter.
productBlurbs.j-508: Seven open seats and 56 jets in the J5 shell, without the extra footprint of the J-509. Households on the older streets of Bowmanville where three generations share one roof pick it, because open seating lets whoever gets home last choose a spot without waiting for a lounger. True Water care with ProClarity 6-Stage filtration means the water is ready at any hour with no prep. Priced at $35,695 on sale at the Dundas Street East showroom.
productBlurbs.j-508l: Same price as the J-508 but one seat fewer and four more jets: the J-508L is for the couple in Brooklin who want the deepest massage Jacuzzi builds rather than the most seats. After the 407 run home from Markham, 60 jets across six positions is the whole point. ProClarity 6-Stage filtration handles the water so a weekday soak needs nothing beyond lifting the cover. Listed at $35,695 during the sale.
productBlurbs.j-408: A seven seat J4 with 41 jets and SmartTub app control, so a commuter on the Lakeshore East line can raise the water temperature from the train and step into it at home. Open seating suits a Seaton family where the kids bring friends and nobody wants to negotiate a lounger. ProClarity 5-Stage filtration keeps maintenance to a weekly check. At $29,995 on sale it is the J4 for a first Jacuzzi buyer who wants app control without the J5 price.
productBlurbs.j-408l: Pickering commuters who drive the 401 to Scarborough and want one full length lounger waiting at the end of it choose the J-408L over the J-408: same $29,995 sale price, one fewer seat, and a lounge that takes the back and legs at once. Six seats still cover a family. Nudge the set point up from the office with the SmartTub app and the True Water system has it clear when you walk in the gate.
productBlurbs.j-404l: Retirees in the lakeside bungalows around Frenchman's Bay do not need seven seats. They need a lounger, a second seat for a partner and a shell that tucks beside the garage out of the wind off the lake. The J-404L gives four seats and 32 jets in a J4 footprint that goes down most older side yards on a dolly. App control and ProClarity 5-Stage filtration come along. Sale price is $25,195.
productBlurbs.j-495: Nine seats is the whole team's parents after a Sunday morning at the arena, and the J-495 is Jacuzzi's largest J-400 with 71 jets in an open layout. A 2025 floor model is on clearance at $31,395 while it lasts. It needs a deep yard, so a hamlet lot in Hampton with a long driveway to the back, or anywhere a truck can reach the pad, is where it fits best. SmartTub app and ProClarity 5-Stage filtration are standard.
productBlurbs.j-485: Uxbridge acreage buyers who want a big, quiet tub for after the barn chores lean toward the J-485: seven open seats, 49 jets and a J-400 shell built to hold heat through moraine winters that bring more snow than the lakeshore. It shares a $30,795 sale price with the J-475 but trades the lounger for a seventh seat, the right call when grandchildren visit. Ask about the 2025 floor model clearance on this one as well.
productBlurbs.j-475: Same J-400 shell as the J-485, but the J-475 puts a lounger in and spreads 55 jets across seven seats. Commuters coming home off the 407 to a crescent near the 412 take the lounger and everyone else takes the open seats. A 2025 floor model is on clearance at $26,295 if you are happy with the unit that has been running on our Dundas Street East floor. The app and the 5-Stage filtration come with it.
productBlurbs.j-445: Dual income households in Courtice who already paid for the deck and the fence look at the J-445 floor model clearance at $23,995 first: a six seat open J-400 with 45 jets, app control and a full Jacuzzi warranty on 2025 stock. The shell width goes through most subdivision gates once a fence panel comes out. No lounger means more room for two adults and two kids on a school night.
productBlurbs.j-435: For a nurse coming off nights at Lakeridge Health the lounger in the J-435 is the reason to buy: 47 jets, six seats, and the SmartTub app to bring the water up from the parking lot. Priced at $27,895 on sale, with a 2025 floor model on clearance as well. Against the J-445 you give up one open seat and gain the full body lounge, and most shift workers take the lounge.
productBlurbs.j-385: Bowmanville families with a north side new build, a forty five foot yard and a budget that stops short of the J-400 series are pointed toward the J-385. It is $26,595 on sale, with 51 jets in an open seven seat layout and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen water care that keeps up with a house full of teenagers. The ProClear skimming weir catches the clippings that fresh sod sheds all summer.
productBlurbs.j-365: Port Perry lake lots where the grandchildren arrive every second weekend do well with the J-365: seven open seats at $24,795 on sale, 46 jets, and a J-300 shell that holds heat when the wind comes across Lake Scugog. The ProCatch bag is simple to rinse, which matters when the tub is filled from a well and the first fill carries iron. Five jets fewer than the J-385 and a step down in price.
productBlurbs.j-345: Parents of Ontario Tech and Durham College students in north Oshawa buy the J-345 because Thanksgiving fills all seven seats and the rest of the year two people use it. Forty one jets and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen come standard, and at $23,195 on sale it is the least expensive seven seat Jacuzzi with True Water care. Open seating means no argument over who gets the lounger, because there is none.
productBlurbs.j-375: Fifty two jets is the most in any six seat J-300, and the J-375 wraps them around a lounger for the Pickering commuter who wants neck, back and calves worked at once after the 401 crawl from Scarborough. Five other seats wait for the family. It is $25,295 on sale, fits behind a house in the Finch Avenue subdivisions without a crane, and the J-355 is the option if jet count matters less than price.
productBlurbs.j-355: North Ajax households above Rossland Road, where the 200 amp panel sits in the basement and the gate is in the side fence, pick the J-355 as the six seat lounger that lands at $24,795 on sale. Forty four jets, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen and a Smart Seal cover that stays put in the southwest wind off the lake. A short electrical run and a fence panel out for the afternoon is the usual install.
productBlurbs.j-335: Six seats, one lounger, 42 jets and $21,995 on sale: this is the tub a Whitby commuter household most often ends up with. It sits between a starter tub and the J-400 series, small enough for a forty foot new build lot and big enough that two adults and two kids do not bump knees. Under a locked cover it holds temperature from the morning GO train to the evening one, so nobody thinks about it.
productBlurbs.j-325: Five open seats and 23 jets keep the J-325 simple, and simple is what a retired couple on a Newcastle village lot wants: room for the neighbours, a quick weekly check of the ProCatch bag, and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen doing the water work. The sale price is $20,495. The shell is smaller than the six seat J-335, so a narrower gate or a tight deck corner near the marina is less of a problem.
productBlurbs.j-315: Older Oshawa streets near the harbour have four foot side yards, and the three seat J-315 is the Jacuzzi that fits down them on a dolly. A lounger plus two seats and 23 jets suit a couple rather than a crowd. It carries the same J-300 shell, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen and ProClear filtration as the big tubs, at $18,795 on sale. For app control in a small footprint look at the four seat J-404L instead.
productBlurbs.j-285: Value seven seater is the honest description: 42 jets, open seating and CLEARRAY UV-C water care at $18,695 on sale. Newcastle families who moved east along the 401 for a detached house and want a Jacuzzi with a full house of seats, without J-300 money, land here. ProClassic 2-Stage filtration with the ProCatch bag is easy to keep up on a rural fill. There is no app, so keep it at temperature rather than reheating from cold.
productBlurbs.j-245: Seven seats for $16,295 on sale is why the J-245 goes to first time buyers in the Bowmanville subdivisions north of the 418, where the mortgage is new and the deck is still on the list. Open seating, 37 jets, CLEARRAY UV-C and the Jacuzzi warranty. It sits five jets short of the J-285 and a step down in price. A 240V circuit from the basement panel is the only prep beyond the pad.
productBlurbs.j-275: While 2025 stock lasts the J-275 is on flash clearance from $14,695, which makes it the lowest priced Jacuzzi lounger on our floor. Six seats, 38 jets and CLEARRAY UV-C water care. Grandparents who followed the family east to Clarington and want one lounge seat plus room for the grandchildren get a lot of tub for the money. Delivery through a subdivision gate is straightforward with the J-200 shell. Once the clearance units are gone, that price goes with them.
productBlurbs.j-235: A six seat lounger at $16,295 on sale, the J-235 is the J-200 pick for a semi off Taunton Road where the yard is narrow and the budget is firm. Thirty four jets, one lounge, CLEARRAY UV-C and a shell slim enough for a dolly delivery past the garage. Same price as the seven seat J-245; choose this one if a lounger matters more than the seventh seat. It runs on a 240V circuit.
productBlurbs.j-225: For a townhome patio near Ajax GO the J-225 is a sensible first Jacuzzi: five open seats, 26 jets, CLEARRAY UV-C and a footprint that fits a fenced patio with the cover lifter against the fence. It is $14,695 on sale. Commuters who want to be soaking twenty minutes after the train pulls in get exactly that, and the ProCatch bag makes the weekly clean quick.
productBlurbs.j-215: Smallest Jacuzzi we carry and, at $14,095 on sale, the least expensive: the J-215 has three seats, one of them a lounger, and 21 jets. It suits a couple in a condo townhouse a short walk from the GO station with a patio rather than a yard. The narrow shell goes down a side passage without lifting a fence panel. CLEARRAY UV-C keeps the water clear on a small volume that heats quickly.
productBlurbs.retreat-all-in-110v: Scugog Island cottages with a hydro service that is already spoken for get the Nordic Retreat All-In-110V: five seats, 13 jets and a 110V 15A GFCI cord that plugs into a dedicated outlet, no panel upgrade and no trench down a long drive. At $9,195 on sale, or from $18.62 bi-weekly OAC, it is the round tub that turns a three season cottage into a year round one. Nordic Clean ozone is easy on a well water fill.
productBlurbs.sport-all-in-110v: Lowest priced tub on the site at $7,295 on sale, or from $15.01 bi-weekly OAC, the Nordic Sport All-In-110V plugs into a standard outlet and seats five with 15 jets. GM shift workers who want a soak after nights without a hydro project get it delivered and running the same day. A round shell rolls through a gate a rectangular tub would not. Built in Michigan, so parts are never far away.
productBlurbs.retreat-se: Step up from the 110V Nordics to the Retreat SE and the 220V 40A service lifts the jet count to 29 across five seats, with a heater that keeps pace on a January night. Townhome owners with a 40A circuit to spare pick it as a round tub that fits a patio corner. It is $10,195 on sale, from $19.38 bi-weekly OAC. Nordic Pure ozone water care keeps the chemical routine light.
productBlurbs.ontario-s106: Two 6-HP jet pumps behind 59 jets, seven open seats, Thermal Shield insulation and a USA built shell: the Wellness Shop Ontario S106 is what a Clarington farm family buys when they want the big tub without the Jacuzzi price. It is $17,695 on sale. The 50 sq ft flow-through filter and ozone system suit a rural fill with a filter on the hose. It is our own label, and it sits filled on the showroom floor beside the J-385 for a direct comparison.
productBlurbs.ontario-s104: Tradespeople who work across Durham and Toronto and want a seven seater that just works pick the Ontario S104 at $15,595 on sale: 54 jets driven by two 6-HP pumps, open seating, Thermal Shield insulation against the damp cold off Lake Ontario, and a flow-through filter. It gives up five jets to the S106 and costs less. Built in the USA for a 60 Hz North American service, it goes on a standard 240V circuit.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s103: Lounger version of the Wellness Shop series, the Ontario L S103 has six seats including a full lounge, 51 jets and two 6-HP pumps, at $15,595 on sale. A couple with a house in the Taunton corridor where the sod is fresh and there are no trees yet get a lounge on a Jacuzzi J-200 budget, with Thermal Shield insulation against the wind across an open yard. Ozone water care with a flow-through filter keeps the weekly routine short.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s105: Top of the Ontario line, the L S105 adds the GECKO K1000 keypad and 56 jets to the six seat lounger layout, with the same two 6-HP pumps and Thermal Shield insulation as the S103. Courtice parents who come home from rink duty most weeknights and want a strong lounge massage at $17,695 on sale get more pump than anything near the price. USA built, ozone water care, a standard 240V hookup.
productBlurbs.the-brook: Four seats, 23 jets and $10,995 on sale with White Glove delivery and setup included, worth up to $1,900: The Brook is the lowest cost route to a full size European built tub for a first home in Seaton, where the yard is small and the budget went to closing costs. Ozone water care, an open layout and a Superior Wellness shell. If you need seven seats at close to this price, see The Cove.
productBlurbs.the-cove: Seven seats for $11,995 on sale, with White Glove delivery and setup included: The Cove is the least expensive seven seater we carry, and it goes to retirees who left Scarborough for a Clarington hamlet like Hampton or Enniskillen and want room for the whole family at Christmas. Twenty seven jets and an ozone system keep it simple. European built by Superior Wellness, and running on our floor so you can sit in it first.
productBlurbs.the-calma: NaturaBalance is the Aquasolus step up, and The Calma is its seven seater with 37 jets, at $13,995 on sale with White Glove delivery included. Courtice families choose it when the fence and deck already ate the budget, and it gives ten more jets than The Cove for the extra spend. Open seating, ozone water care, European build. A gate wide enough for the shell on its edge is all the yard needs, and our crew confirms that before delivery day.
productBlurbs.the-eden: Same $13,995 sale price as The Calma, but The Eden trades a seat for a lounger and takes 42 jets, the most in the Aquasolus range. A couple in a north Ajax new build who want a lounge without going to a Jacuzzi J-200 get one here, with White Glove delivery and setup included and an ozone system. Superior Wellness builds it in Europe. It is filled and warm on the Dundas Street East floor for a wet test.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-powerpro: Flagship of the swim spa range, the J-19DT PowerPro runs 19 feet with dual temperature: a swim end with the PowerPro current and a separate hot tub end that stays at soaking heat while the lane sits cooler for training. Six seats, 53 jets, Quad 50 sq ft filtration. It needs a deep lot and a crane, so rural Scugog and the acreage north of Orono are where it lands. Triathletes training for open water season on Lake Ontario get a real lane. $60,895 on sale.
productBlurbs.j-19-powerpro: A single temperature 19 footer for the swimmer who cares about the lane more than the lounge: the J-19 PowerPro gives the strongest current Jacuzzi makes, four seats and 34 jets, at $58,995 on sale. Masters swimmers from the Pickering waterfront who want to train at home in February choose it over the J-19DT when they do not need a second hot zone. One 40A circuit and a reinforced slab, and we plan the lift at a site visit.
productBlurbs.j-16-powerpro: Sixteen feet is the length that fits an older Oshawa lot without giving up the rest of the yard, and the J-16 PowerPro keeps the full PowerPro swim current in that length. Four seats, 34 jets, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen with dual 50 sq ft filters. Runners who want low impact cross training through the winter buy it. $54,295 on sale, a single 40A circuit, and room for a walkway beside it.
productBlurbs.j-14-powerpro: Strong current in the short shell: the J-14 PowerPro is 14 feet, five seats, 51 jets and the PowerPro swim system, at $48,795 on sale. It is the swim spa for a Brooklin new build where the rear yard measures under thirty feet and a pool was never on the table. Set it parallel to the rear fence with the crane on the street. Dual 50 sq ft filtration and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen keep the water clear year round.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-poweractive: Dual temperature at $53,295 on sale, the J-19DT PowerActive gives a family the separate hot tub zone of the J-19DT PowerPro with a slightly gentler current and a lower price. Six seats, 51 jets, four 50 sq ft filters. On a Port Perry lake lot the kids swim in the cool end while the adults soak in the hot one. Two circuits, 20A and 40A, and a crane delivery that we schedule for firm ground.
productBlurbs.j-19-poweractive: Nineteen feet of lane at $51,395 on sale, the J-19 PowerActive is for the family that wants length for laps and lessons more than a race current. Four seats, 32 jets, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen. Newcastle village lots that run back to a rear garage take it easily, and a boater who splits summer between the harbour and the yard gets an off season swim. A single 40A circuit runs it.
productBlurbs.j-16-poweractive: Middle of the Jacuzzi range on every count, the J-16 PowerActive at $46,495 on sale is 16 feet, four seats, 32 jets and a PowerActive current that suits swimmers working on technique and adults who want low impact exercise. Central Pickering lots between the 401 and Finch Avenue, wide and level, are ideal for it. A 16 footer leaves room for a sauna beside it, and it draws from one 40A circuit.
productBlurbs.j-14-poweractive: At $41,395 on sale the J-14 PowerActive is the swim spa that replaced the pool on more than one forty foot lot in Courtice. Fourteen feet, five seats, 49 jets and the PowerActive current: enough to swim against for fitness, with a hot tub level of jets for the soak afterward. It sits along the fence line on a reinforced slab and runs off one 40A circuit from the basement panel.
productBlurbs.j-13-powerplay: Eight seats in 13 feet makes the J-13 PowerPlay less a training lane and more a warm pool for a family, which is what Brooklin parents with three kids and no room for an in-ground pool are after. Thirty eight jets, a 32A circuit and a 50 sq ft DFML filter. It is $33,195 on sale. Swim against the current for exercise, then the whole family sits down. The short shell makes delivery day quick.
productBlurbs.j-12-flow: Entry to the swim spa range at $30,695 on sale, the J-12 Flow is 12 feet, eight seats, 31 jets and CLEARRAY UV-C water care with a 50 sq ft DFML filter. Whitby families near the Thickson corridor who want a place the kids can play in July and everyone can soak in January choose it over a hot tub plus a pool. One 32A circuit. A foot shorter than the J-13 PowerPlay, so it fits a tighter yard.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-dualstream-19: Two pools in one shell: the SwimExpert DualStream 19 pairs a 19 foot swim lane with 53 jets and an attached five person hot tub with 30 jets and its own controls, at $56,095 on sale. ClearStream mineral water care means fewer chemicals across both zones. On the moraine acreage around Uxbridge, where the yard is measured in acres, it gives one household a lane for the athlete and a hot tub for everyone else. Two circuits, one crane.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-aquastream-17: Seventeen feet is a length Jacuzzi does not build, and the SwimExpert AquaStream 17 fills the gap for an Ajax lot that is too short for a 19 footer and too long to settle for 14. Three seats, 30 jets, ClearStream mineral water care and the AquaStream current for lap work. It is $50,095 on sale. Waterfront Trail runners who want a swim after the run get their lane. One 40A circuit and a crane from the street.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-swimstream-14: Serious current in a 14 foot SwimLife shell: the SwimExpert SwimStream 14 has three seats, 30 jets and ClearStream mineral water care at $44,795 on sale. Hobby farmers around Tyrone who want to swim laps without driving to the rec centre put it on a pad by the house. It is the SwimExpert current at the SwimFit length. A 32A circuit is enough to run it.
productBlurbs.swimfit-aquastream-17: SwimFit is the SwimLife value line, and the AquaStream 17 gives 17 feet of swim lane, three seats and 28 jets for $43,795 on sale. A GO commuter who trains for a summer open water swim and wants length without the SwimExpert price picks it. ClearStream mineral water care keeps the chemical routine light. Single 40A circuit. We do a site visit before booking delivery into the Seaton subdivisions.
productBlurbs.swimfit-swimstream-14: At $38,095 on sale the SwimFit SwimStream 14 is the lowest priced swim spa with a proper swim current on our site: 14 feet, three seats, 28 jets, ClearStream mineral care. A semi on the newer streets of Newcastle toward the harbour, with a wider than usual yard, takes it on a slab along the fence. The J-12 Flow has more seats; this one has the better lane. A 32A circuit runs it.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-1: One person, full spectrum infrared, $10,495 on sale, and right now a free AROMA ONE aromatherapy diffuser comes with it. The Sanctuary 1 fits where a treadmill would in an Ajax townhome basement and runs on a household circuit, so no electrician. Paramedics and nurses at Lakeridge Health who want twenty minutes of heat after a shift buy it for themselves. True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-2: Two people side by side in a cabin that plugs into a standard outlet: the Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 on sale is the infrared sauna we deliver into more Brooklin basements than any other. It assembles in an afternoon in the corner of an unfinished basement with no renovation. Full spectrum True Wave heaters, low EMF, Basswood or Mahogany. Pair it with a Chill Tubs plunge for contrast; we quote both together at the showroom.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-3: Three seats gives a family room for two adults and a teenager in the Sanctuary 3, at $12,995 on sale. It is the step up for a Courtice basement where the sauna will be shared, and one of the cabins we most often deliver beside a cold plunge. Full spectrum infrared with True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, lifetime warranty on the cabin and heaters. Send us ceiling height and door width and we will confirm the fit.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-5: Five seats make the Sanctuary 5 the family cabin of the Clearlight line, at $13,995 on sale, so nobody's knees touch even with the whole household inside. A Bowmanville home with a finished basement rec room that wants the sauna to feel like a room rather than a booth chooses it over the Sanctuary 3. Full spectrum infrared, True Wave heaters, low EMF, Basswood or Mahogany, and the lifetime cabin and heater warranty. It arrives as flat panels and is assembled in place.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-y: Four seats at $13,995 on sale, the Sanctuary Y is the cabin for a household in north Oshawa where the sauna gets shared: a couple, an adult child home from Durham College and a friend. Full spectrum infrared, True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters. Shift workers coming off nights at GM use it at odd hours without waking anyone. It costs the same as the three seat Sanctuary 5 and adds a seat.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-c: Corner footprint is the reason the Sanctuary C goes into finished basements in Whitby where the floor space is already assigned to a TV and a treadmill. Four seats at $14,495 on sale, full spectrum True Wave infrared, Basswood or Mahogany, lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters. Cyclists who ride the Waterfront Trail through a cold spring use it to warm up after the ride, and it tucks into the angle two walls make.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-retreat: Top of the Clearlight range at $15,295 on sale, the Sanctuary Retreat seats four in a full height cabin, with full spectrum True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, and the lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters. It suits the deep lots and big basements of old Newcastle, where a couple who host the extended family want a sauna that seats guests. Equestrians from the Uxbridge farms use it after a cold morning in the barn.
productBlurbs.serenity-mini: Compact Canadian-made cedar, the Serenity Mini is priced at $14,995 on sale in knotty cedar with clear cedar available, heater sold separately. Up to 194°F with steam, it is the traditional outdoor sauna for a village lot in Port Perry where the yard has room for a small cabin beside the tub. Choose electric if a 240V line is close, wood burning if it is not. The panels pass through a standard gate one at a time.
productBlurbs.serenity-sauna: Full size Serenity Sauna, $17,495 on sale, is the wood fired sauna we deliver to north Clarington farms and the moraine lots around Uxbridge, where running hydro to the back of the property costs more than the heater. Canadian-made Western red cedar, knotty at the shown price or clear cedar for a step up, open bench, up to 194°F with water on the rocks. The heater is sold separately so you pick electric or wood.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-bath: Lie back, shoulders under, and let the chiller hold the water cold through a Durham July when a hose fill will not: the Chill Tub Essential Bath is the open tub layout of the Chill Tubs range, the one most people picture. GM shift workers who want a contrast routine after a Clearlight session put it on the garage floor beside the cabin. Pricing is at the showroom, and we quote it alongside a Sanctuary 2 or 3.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-pod: Upright rather than reclined, the Chill Tub Essential Pod takes less floor area than the Essential Bath, which is why it goes onto the patios of Ajax townhomes and into the corner of a Seaton garage. You sit with the water to your neck. Lacrosse and hockey players across Durham use it after games. Pricing is at the showroom, where the pod is set up and running so you can see the chiller and the controls.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-obsidian: Step up in finish and build from the Essential models, the Chill Tub Obsidian has a dark shell that sits well against a cedar sauna on a Scugog waterfront lot. It is for the buyer who wants the plunge to look like part of the yard rather than a piece of gym equipment. Pricing is at the showroom. Come stand beside it on the Dundas Street East floor and compare it to the Essential Bath.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-pro: Built for people who plunge every day, the Chill Tub Pro is the top of the range, sized and equipped for a household of athletes, whether that is a Whitby family with three kids in rep hockey or a masters swimmer who trains in the lake all summer. It is the model we pair with the Sanctuary Y for a full contrast setup. Pricing is at the showroom, and the floor unit is running so you can check the water temperature yourself.
productBlurbs.summit-ws190: Top massage chair we stock, the Wellness Shop Summit WS190 earns its place on the drive home: an hour on the 401 from Scarborough to Clarington leaves a back that a full body program undoes in twenty minutes. It goes in a family room or a finished basement, plugs into a standard outlet, and the only prep is measuring the doorway. Pricing is at the showroom, where both chairs are set up to try.
productBlurbs.dreamcatcher-ws170: More compact of our two Wellness Shop chairs, the Dreamcatcher WS170 is sized for a condo townhouse near the Whitby GO or a den in an Oshawa bungalow where the Summit WS190 would take too much floor. Nurses off a Lakeridge Health shift try it on our floor and decide in five minutes. Pricing is at the showroom, and we suggest sitting in both back to back before choosing.
productBlurbs.duke-series: Enclosed veranda style is the Duke Series: western red cedar with screened walls, and it is what a hot tub owner on the Bay Ridges streets by the lake buys to get out of the wind and the bugs at once. Multiple sizes cover a tub alone or a tub with a sitting area. It goes on the same base as the tub. Pricing is at the showroom, where we walk you through the sizes and options.
productBlurbs.cypress-series: Cedar panel walls make the Cypress Series read as a small outbuilding, and on a Newcastle village lot with a rear garage it ties the tub in with the rest of the yard. Multiple sizes, western red cedar throughout, with room for a change area beside the tub. Cedar takes the freezing rain season better than a fabric canopy. Pricing is at the showroom; bring your tub model and yard measurements.
productBlurbs.hudson-series: Built around the full size hot tub, the Hudson Series is an enclosed cedar gazebo starting at 11 by 14 feet and going up from there, with room for a seven seater and a bench for towels. Retirees on a Port Perry lake lot who want to soak through freezing rain without walking out in it choose an enclosed design. Western red cedar, built by Visscher. Pricing is at the showroom, where the Duke and Hudson are compared side by side.
productBlurbs.sequoia-11-14: Open-air and louvered, the Sequoia 11 by 14 has cedar posts, a roof that adjusts and no walls, so a Brooklin new build with neighbours on both sides gets shade over the tub by day and a view of the sky at night. It sits over a hot tub or the seating end of a swim spa. Western red cedar by Visscher. Pricing is at the showroom, and we size the base for tub and gazebo together.

financingFaq.q: What does 0% for 12 months OAC actually cover?
financingFaq.a: On approved credit, you pay no interest on the bi-weekly payments for the first year. How long the balance is amortized depends on the product, and longer terms at regular rates are available if you want a smaller payment. Approval is based on your credit profile and usually comes back within minutes.

financingFaq.q: Where does the bi-weekly number on each product page come from?
financingFaq.a: It is the advertised starting payment for that model at today's sale price under the 0% for 12 months promotion, on approved credit. The amortization behind it varies by product, so two tubs at similar prices can show slightly different payments. The Whitby team can adjust the term or the payment frequency when you apply.

financingFaq.q: Can the cover, steps and delivery go on the same payment?
financingFaq.a: Yes. Covers, lifters, steps, start-up chemicals and any in-store bundle can be rolled into one financed amount along with delivery. The one exception is the electrical hookup, which your licensed electrician quotes and bills separately.

financingFaq.q: Do I need money down to take a tub home?
financingFaq.a: Usually not. On approved credit most buyers put nothing down and start with the first bi-weekly payment. If you prefer to put something toward it to lower the payment, tell the team at Dundas Street East and they will run both versions.

buyCanadian.pageLead: Buy Canadian is more than a sticker on the tub. The company taking your deposit is based in Ontario, the crew that carries the tub around the side of the house lives in Durham, and the technician who answers a January service call comes from Whitby, not a call centre.
body: The Wellness Shop started as a single local hot tub store and has grown over 25 years into eight showrooms across Ontario. Whitby covers all of Durham Region, from Pickering through Oshawa and Clarington, with staff who commute on the same 401 you do. Nothing about the sale, the delivery or the warranty work leaves the province.

The brands are the ones you already know. We are an authorized Jacuzzi dealer, so every J-200 through J-500 carries the full factory warranty. Serenity saunas are built in Canada from Western red cedar. Our Wellness Shop Ontario series was specified for the winters that blow in off Lake Ontario, with full foam insulation and heavy covers. Choosing to buy Canadian here means choosing where the money and the service live, not giving up the brand you wanted.

The part that pays off is the decade after delivery. Filter changes, cover replacements, a heater under warranty: all of it runs through the Whitby showroom with parts on hand and a crew that has already been to your address once.

faq.q: Is the Wellness Shop a Canadian company?
faq.a: Yes. The Wellness Shop is an Ontario company that grew from one local hot tub store into eight showrooms across the province, including the Whitby showroom on Dundas Street East serving Durham Region. Sales, delivery and service are handled by Ontario staff.

faq.q: Are your hot tubs made in Canada?
faq.a: Serenity outdoor saunas are built in Canada from Western red cedar. Jacuzzi and our Wellness Shop Ontario series hot tubs are built in the United States, Nordic in Michigan and Aquasolus in Europe. Every one is sold by a Canadian company and delivered and serviced by the Whitby team.
